messages:
Maya Singh: ACME's security team asked for a short IR + breach notify blurb they can include in the POC SOW. They want timelines, what artifacts we'll share on hosted vs VPC, and a simple escalation matrix. Can we draft?
Carlos Perez: I can draft. Quick clarification: POC is on hosted API for now, right?
Maya Singh: Correct, hosted. They asked for both hosted behavior and what changes if they move to VPC later.
Ruth Adler: For hosted we can commit to notification windows but not host-level access. Suggested language: 
```
Incident Notification: Redwood will notify the Customer of confirmed security incidents impacting Customer data within 72 hours of confirmation. For incidents classified as High/Sev1 (e.g., confirmed data exfiltration), Redwood will provide an initial notification within 24 hours and follow up updates at least every 48 hours until remediation. Redwood will preserve relevant request logs and metadata for 90 days. Access to host images, raw disks, or VM snapshots is only available for Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments and requires a separate agreement.
```
LegalBot: Add evidence custody line: "Redwood may retain copies of forensic artifacts for investigation but will not disclose Customer content except as required by law or authorized by Customer."
Carlos Perez: For the SOW escalation snippet, keep role emails rather than personal. Draft: 
```
POC Escalation (Hosted):
- CS: cs@redwood.com
- Solutions Eng: solutions@redwood.com
- Security (notification): security@redwood.com
- Legal & Contracts: contracts@redwood.com
```
Ruth Adler: Also include forensic scope note: we will provide request traces, API logs, and any preserved cached artifacts relevant to the incident. For deeper forensic access (host-level snapshots, process memory), customer must use Dedicated/Private.
Maya Singh: ACME asked if we will update their SIG/CAIQ entry after an incident (they want transparency).
LegalBot: We can offer to update CAIQ/SIG rows for named customers as part of post-incident communications with the customer's consent; include this as an optional line in the SOW.
Carlos Perez: Short summary for their SOW: "Redwood will notify confirmed incidents within 72 hours (24 hours for high severity), preserve request-level logs for 90 days, and coordinate forensic activities with the Customer. Host-level imaging is only supported on Dedicated/Private deployments. Role-based contacts will be used for POC; enterprise agreements can specify named responders and tighter SLAs."
Maya Singh: Great. @sec-bot please attach the public IR docs.
sec-bot: <https://redwood.com/security/incident-response>
Maya Singh: Sending this to ACME now. Will escalate if they push for a 48-hour non-negotiable for hosted. :thumbsup:
